transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Marquez (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (CTO, Cerulean Health), Liam O'Neill (Head of MLOps), Rosa Nguyen (VP Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): walked through model catalog, open models, benchmarks, deployment options, customer asks for VPC/HIPAA guardrails, request for pilot and benchmark spreadsheet.

00:00 Sophie Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um i'm sophie from redwood, i'll kick us off, we got about 50 minutes, carlos will do the deep dive on the model catalog and benchmarks
00:14 Dr. Maya Patel: thanks sophie, excited to see this, we are evaluating open models for our clinical summarization workflows and want to understand latency/cost trade offs
00:27 Sophie Chen: great, quick intro, redwood provides a catalog of vetted open models, with perf profiles, compatibility notes (quantized variants, seq length limits), and recommended runtimes - we support hosted API, dedicated pools, and private VPC deployments
00:43 Carlos Marquez: quick note, i'll show the catalog UI and then the compatibility matrix we use to map models to runtime/quantization and GPU/kernel support - some names may be transcribed wrong in the export, sorry in advance
01:05 Rosa Nguyen: one big question - do you have HIPAA / SOC2 controls? we need encryption at rest with our KMS, audit logs, and SSO for access controls
01:18 Sophie Chen: yes, we have SOC 2 type II, KMS integration and audit logs, SSO via SAML/OIDC; for private you can bring your HSM or cloud KMS, we'll share the compliance pack after the call
01:31 Liam O'Neill: for the pilot we care about 99th p99 latency under 300ms for single-turn summaries, and cost per 1k tokens under $X, roughly. also need to know if prefix caching/KV cache helps us
01:46 Carlos Marquez: yep, so in the catalog you'll see per-model benchmarks: p50/p95/p99 latencies for typical prompt lengths, tokens per second throughput, and cost estimates under hosted vs dedicated. caching (KV cache) and batching settings are noted - sometimes shows as 'KV cash' in transcripts lol
02:06 Sophie Chen: okay carlos, show the model catalog please
02:12 Carlos Marquez: pulling up the UI. So first tile is the 'gpt-open-7b' family - we've benchmarked fp16, int8 and a quantized 4-bit variant. The compatibility matrix indicates which runtime kernels we use and which GPUs are recommended; e.g., for int8 on T4s expect higher latency but lower cost, on A100 you get better latency/cost mix
03:00 Carlos Marquez: here on the right you can filter by use case, like summarization, retrieval-augmented, and by constraints (latency SLO, max sequence length). the matrix column 'compatibility' will say if the model supports KV caching, prefix caching, and whether we have a Redwood-verified quantized build
03:28 Dr. Maya Patel: in your benchmarks, where is the test promptset coming from? we need to know if it's representative of our clinical notes which are long and have structured fields
03:40 Carlos Marquez: good question - default bench uses our public workload mixes but for pilots we run your prompt set. the spreadsheet we send will have the raw latency traces and hardware used, so you can verify
04:02 Rosa Nguyen: can you show an example compatibility matrix row for a model that is both high quality and fast?
04:10 Carlos Marquez: sure - for 'mosaic-mantle-7b' we have fp16 on A100: p50~70ms, p95~150ms, p99~220ms for 512 token prompts. int8/4bit on T4 gives p50~120ms, p95~300ms. quality-wise the evals on our internal eval suite show minimal degradation for 4bit quant with calibration sets
04:45 Liam O'Neill: are the evals tied to prompt sets? can we re-run evals when we change prompts and detect regressions?
04:54 Sophie Chen: yes, we have Redwood Optimize that ties prompt sets/evals to monitoring; you can setup regression alerts and automatic rollback on a canary rollout if quality dips
05:10 Carlos Marquez: one note about compatibility: some older kernels don't support KV cache eviction well, so for long sequences we recommend models flagged as 'seq-optimized' - we'll indicate that in the matrix
05:30 Dr. Maya Patel: regarding private deployment - do you support on-prem air-gapped? we have some PHI that we'd rather keep inside our VPC for the pilot if possible
05:42 Sophie Chen: yes, private deployment supports VPC and on-prem packages; for air-gapped we do an install bundle and work with your infra team. audit logs and KMS/HSM integrations are part of that offering
06:00 Carlos Marquez: back to the UI - you can compare models side-by-side: quality scores (our eval metrics), cost per 1k tokens, and runtime compatibility. there's also a 'recommended for production' badge when a model passes stability tests across multiple runtimes
06:30 Rosa Nguyen: are the model versions pinned? we don't want silent model upgrades breaking things in prod
06:36 Sophie Chen: yes customers can pin model versions and use rollout policies (canary, A/B) to control upgrades. we also surface changelogs and performance diffs in the console
07:00 Liam O'Neill: what about multi-turn chat and KV cache growth? our summaries sometimes use conversation history ~2k tokens
07:10 Carlos Marquez: we show KV cache memory growth estimates in the matrix - some quantized builds have smaller KV sizes; we also recommend LRU eviction policies for long multiparty threads. note: sometimes transcription mixes KV cache with 'KV cash' - ignore that
07:32 Dr. Maya Patel: on benchmarks - do you provide raw traces for p99 spikes? we need to see the variance under load and tail behavior for multi-tenant hosted setups
07:45 Carlos Marquez: absolutely; in hosted we can break down token-level latency, and for dedicated we provide per-node traces. the benchmark spreadsheet includes p50/p95/p99 and raw per-request samples
08:10 Sophie Chen: let's talk pricing briefly - hosted is usage-based per token, dedicated is reserved capacity with committed monthly units; Optimize features like advanced observability are add-ons
08:25 Rosa Nguyen: curious about unit economics - if we move to dedicated, what's the expected break-even for our load? we can share traffic profiles
08:35 Sophie Chen: we'll model that in the pricing sheet; dedicated typically makes sense above sustained throughput thresholds - we'll include a cost model in the spreadsheet Carlos will share
08:50 Carlos Marquez: a quick demo of compatibility edge cases: some community forks use custom attention layers that break standard exporter paths; our onboarding flags those and recommends a compatible fork or a conversion step
09:20 Liam O'Neill: do you support model compilation steps (like operator fusion) and kernel selection automatically? we use mixed hardware fleet so routing matters
09:30 Carlos Marquez: yes, the runtime auto-selects kernels and compiles when needed; the matrix lists supported backends per model so you can see which GPUs/compilers were used in bench runs
09:48 Dr. Maya Patel: security question: does Redwood ever see raw prompt/response content in private deployment? we need guarantees about data residency
09:58 Sophie Chen: for private deployments you control the control plane and data plane; Redwood-managed hosted API will see metadata for billing but we can limit or disable telemetry. we'll provide the data handling spec in the security pack
10:20 Rosa Nguyen: any red flags around hallucination for clinical summarization? we need to measure factuality
10:28 Carlos Marquez: we run automated factuality suites and your custom prompt tests during the pilot; Optimize allows you to set quality thresholds and trigger alerts on drift
10:45 Sophie Chen: switching back to the UI, there's a downloadable compatibility matrix CSV link - we'll attach that in the follow-up (link: https://redwood.example/model-catalog/compatibility.csv)
11:02 Liam O'Neill: perfect, for the pilot we'll want a benchmark run against our prompt set using both hosted and dedicated to compare p99 and cost
11:12 Carlos Marquez: agreed, we'll run hosted and dedicated variants, and include an A100 and T4-based run if you want - that will show cost/latency differences
11:30 Dr. Maya Patel: timeline - if we get the spreadsheet and the pricing by next week, we can kick off the pilot the week after, aiming to decide by end of month
11:45 Sophie Chen: noted, i'll send the security pack and pricing. carlos will send the bench spreadsheet + matrix. lian? liam?
11:55 Liam O'Neill: i'll share the prompt set today and traffic snapshot by tomorrow
12:05 Rosa Nguyen: ok that works for us
12:12 Sophie Chen: any final questions?
12:18 Dr. Maya Patel: none from me, thanks for the clear walkthrough
12:22 Sophie Chen: great, recap of next steps: send pricing & security docs, share compatibility matrix & bench raw traces, schedule pilot run week of 2026-12-14. thanks everyone
12:35 End of recording

Notes on transcription quality: medium - some product names and technical terms may be slightly off (e.g., 'KV cash' instead of 'KV cache', 'Redwood Optimise' vs 'Optimize').
